items.title: Enforce experience registry, artifact and design-dependency coverage
items.outcome: A required check proves every frontend ticket, critical journey, screen, state, component, diagram and design artifact has complete ownership and valid dependencies.
items.context: A large screen inventory is not assurance unless drift fails. This is the independent QA consumer of T-UXR-06 rather than the registry author approving itself.
scope: Critical flow independent QA and release-gate coverage
acceptance_criteria: Every Android/web/admin frontend implementation ticket maps to at least one screen/flow and exact design prerequisite
Every critical flow has design, implementation and independent QA owners
No dangling, duplicate, orphan or unused planning record and no unversioned D6 handoff passes
Expired D6/D8 handoff or readiness approval blocks readiness and release
Deliberate missing-screen, missing-state, missing-dependency and bypass fixtures fail with exact IDs
contracts_schema: Consumes experience-coverage.schema.json and D0-D9 gate/approval records
security_privacy: Registry has metadata only
Security-critical flows require denial, revocation and safe-failure states
observability: Coverage percentage and failure count by platform, criticality, owner, state and gate
tests: Negative fixtures for every validation class
rollout_rollback: Warn only until initial registry is complete, then required before any frontend Ready
Rollback retains last valid report and blocks new readiness
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Design QA owns validator assertions and fixtures; DesignOps owns source records and cannot waive failures.
definition_of_done: Required coverage check merged
All negative fixtures fail correctly
Design QA, Architecture and CDO approvals recorded
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Run independent heuristic reviews and cognitive walkthroughs
items.outcome: Independent reviewers find navigation, mental-model, error-prevention, trust and recovery defects across all critical prototypes before participant testing or handoff.
items.context: Design authors cannot reliably audit their own assumptions. Finance-specific heuristics must cover provenance, uncertainty, reversibility and safe failure in addition to generic usability.
scope: Nielsen-style heuristic review adapted to finance/trust
Persona-based cognitive walkthrough for every critical flow
Error prevention, correction, undo and recovery
Severity, evidence, owner and retest disposition
acceptance_criteria: Every critical flow is reviewed by someone who did not author it
Findings cover task clarity, financial comprehension, provenance, uncertainty, authorization and recovery
High/critical findings block D5 and are retested after revision
Cross-platform inconsistency is either corrected or recorded as approved divergence
Review evidence links exact flow/screen/component IDs
contracts_schema: Finding, severity, heuristic, artifact version, affected IDs, disposition and retest records
security_privacy: Synthetic scenarios only
Reviewers have least-privilege artifact access
observability: Findings by severity/heuristic/platform, age and reopen rate
rollout_rollback: Run on D3/D4 versions and rerun affected flows
An expired review blocks D6 rather than falling back to author signoff
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Design QA reviewers divide flows by platform but use one calibrated severity and finding schema.
definition_of_done: All critical flow reviews completed
High/critical findings closed/retested
Design QA Lead accepts calibration and evidence
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Audit prototype accessibility with assistive technology
items.outcome: Critical prototypes are independently evaluated for WCAG 2.2 AA and native Android outcomes using keyboard, screen reader, switch, large text/zoom, contrast and reduced motion before D6.
items.context: Automated contrast checks cannot evaluate reading order, names, cognitive clarity, table alternatives or recovery. Prototype accessibility must precede code.
scope: Semantic structure, names, roles, states and reading order
Largest Android text, 200 percent zoom/reflow and touch targets
Reduced motion, charts/tables, timeouts and errors
acceptance_criteria: Every critical flow has a recorded assistive-technology script and result
No critical/serious accessibility defect remains open at D6
Every chart, visual status and drag/gesture has a text or operable alternative
Focus/Back returns predictably from overlays and errors identify fields plus recovery
Exceptions are criterion-specific, dated, CDO/Accessibility-approved and cannot waive critical paths
contracts_schema: Accessibility finding maps criterion, assistive technology, artifact IDs, severity, owner and retest
security_privacy: Assistive labels do not reveal masked/hidden data
Timeout accommodation never weakens step-up or authorization
observability: Defects by criterion/platform/severity, retest age and exception expiry
rollout_rollback: Runs before participant tests and D6
Failure reopens affected artifact and blocks handoff
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Accessibility specialists test platform prototypes independently and write findings into one evidence model.
definition_of_done: All critical prototype audits/retests complete
No critical/serious open defects
Accessibility Lead and Design QA accept evidence
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Validate Android critical journeys and permission comprehension
items.outcome: Representative users complete Android activation, debt, transaction, clarification and recovery prototypes and understand optional permissions, status and consequences before D6.
items.context: The core wedge depends on Android and sensitive permissions. Task success without permission comprehension or manual fallback is not acceptable.
scope: Offline, constrained-device, largest-text and safe-exit tasks
acceptance_criteria: Each critical task meets the pre-registered success threshold or is revised/retested
Participants explain what each permission grants, what remains local and how to revoke
Deny-everything participants reach first value without coaching
Debt/clarification participants correctly explain source, status and correction consequence
Findings are dispositioned into T-UXA tickets before T-UXA-16
contracts_schema: Study tasks reference Android flow/screen IDs, persona, artifact version, result and finding
security_privacy: Synthetic device/messages only and wipe between participants
Safe-exit participants recruited independently
observability: Task success/time/error, permission comprehension, correction and recovery with no personal financial data
rollout_rollback: Research-only; failed threshold blocks Android D6
Revised flows receive a new artifact version and targeted retest
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Independent UX Research owns sessions; Android designers observe and fix but do not moderate or score their own flows.
definition_of_done: All Android critical tasks tested
Threshold failures revised/retested
Research, Accessibility and Design QA approvals recorded
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Validate customer web bulk, planning and recovery journeys
items.outcome: Representative web users complete auth/recovery, import/bulk, debt/planning, sharing, billing and trust tasks across responsive and keyboard contexts before D6.
items.context: Web's value is dense analysis and bulk work. Prototype validation must prove it is faster and clearer than phone workflows without sacrificing narrow/accessible use.
scope: Billing/trust/export/delete at desktop, narrow width and 200 percent zoom
acceptance_criteria: Each critical task meets pre-registered success/comprehension thresholds or is revised/retested
Import preview and repeat-import safety are understood without coaching
Keyboard-only and 200 percent zoom users complete all tasks
Sharing, billing and deletion consequences are predicted correctly
Findings are dispositioned before T-UXW-12
contracts_schema: Study tasks reference web flow/screen IDs, persona, viewport, input mode, artifact and result
security_privacy: Synthetic data and non-enumerating support scenarios
No real file/account/household data
observability: Task success/time/error, comprehension, navigation and recovery by viewport/input
rollout_rollback: Research-only; failed threshold blocks web D6
Targeted retest follows new artifact version
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Independent researchers run sessions; web designers fix but do not self-score.
definition_of_done: All web critical tasks tested
Threshold failures revised/retested
Research, Accessibility and Design QA approvals recorded

items.title: Validate admin operator accuracy, four-eyes and clock-pressure journeys
items.outcome: Qualified operators complete support, rights, access, plan, provider and incident tasks accurately under denial, unavailable-dependency and time-pressure conditions before D6.
items.context: Operator usability failure can become a security or statutory failure. Testing only cooperative happy paths rewards unsafe shortcuts.
acceptance_criteria: Operators select correct bounded action and can explain why unavailable/denied paths cannot be bypassed
Requestor/self/ineligible approvers are never selected and no task needs hidden knowledge
Clock-pressure tasks escalate safely without unmasking or silently pausing
Keyboard/screen-reader operators complete all critical queues within tested thresholds
Findings are dispositioned before T-UXM-11
contracts_schema: Simulation tasks reference role, flow/screen, policy state, artifact, expected safe outcome and result
security_privacy: Synthetic/redacted cases only and no production access
Observers cannot alter approval outcome
observability: Task accuracy, unsafe attempt, escalation, time and comprehension by role without customer content
rollout_rollback: Research-only; unsafe outcome blocks admin D6
Revised flows receive targeted operator retest
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Design QA facilitates role simulations; admin designers and security observe but do not score their own flows.
definition_of_done: All operator critical tasks tested
Unsafe/threshold failures revised/retested
Security, Compliance, Accessibility and Design QA approve

items.title: Validate financial comprehension, content and localization readiness
items.outcome: Users can explain consequential financial figures, statuses, actions and uncertainty, and every approved layout survives source and pseudo-localized content ranges.
items.context: A completed click path is not success when the user misreads payoff, projected, available, pending, reversed, aggregate or revoked.
scope: Pseudo-localization, long strings, numbers, currencies and bidirectional fixtures
Platform content parity and regulated version coverage
acceptance_criteria: Pre-registered comprehension thresholds pass for every critical money/status term
Participants predict destructive, sharing and billing consequences before confirmation
No layout clips or hides a consequence at maximum pseudo-localized range
Money formatting remains correct and unchanged in value across locale fixtures
Failed terms/layouts are revised and retested before D6
contracts_schema: Comprehension task, term, locale, content range, artifact, threshold, result and finding records
security_privacy: Synthetic figures only
Translation/research artifacts contain no personal or production content
observability: Comprehension and localization defects by term, flow, locale and platform
tests: Banned language and regulated-copy expiry lint
rollout_rollback: Runs before platform D6
Unsupported locale remains disabled rather than using incomplete regulated copy
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Content QA and localization reviewers divide terms/locales and use one result schema.
definition_of_done: Critical comprehension/localization matrix complete
Failures revised/retested
Content, Localization, Accessibility and Design QA approve
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Red-team privacy, coercion, dark-pattern and unsafe operator designs
items.outcome: Adversarial design review proves sharing, billing, permissions, AI and admin flows do not enable surveillance, coercion, manipulation, secret exposure or authorization shortcuts.
items.context: Usability testing with cooperative participants misses the strongest abuse cases. These are interface-enabled harms that must fail before implementation.
scope: Household differencing, grant escalation, access history, revoke and safe exit
acceptance_criteria: Every named abuse scenario has attacker, precondition, attempted path, expected safe outcome and evidence
No aggregate/detail, permission or operator flow exposes a hidden resource or bypass
Cancel/revoke/exit remain no harder than enabling and use no shame or artificial urgency
No secret/raw content or prohibited financial detail appears in any designed state
All high/critical design-abuse findings close and retest before D6
contracts_schema: Design abuse scenario and result records link threat, flow/screen/component, severity, owner and retest
security_privacy: Specialist coercive-control review and independent recruitment
No live household/operator data
observability: Scenario coverage, findings, age and reopen rate without sensitive scenario content
tests: Planted unsafe design controls prove suite detection
rollout_rollback: Runs before platform D6 and on affected changes
Failed/expired evidence disables the feature design gate
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Design security reviewers own abuse scenarios; artifact authors receive findings but cannot alter expected outcomes.
definition_of_done: All abuse scenarios executed
High/critical findings closed/retested
Security, Privacy, Inclusive Design and Design QA approve
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Gate tokens, components, variants and design-system adoption
items.outcome: A required design-system gate catches missing variants, inaccessible tokens, duplicates, detached instances, stale versions and unmapped platform components before D6.
items.context: A published library can still be bypassed or incomplete. Independent lint makes adoption and state coverage measurable.
acceptance_criteria: Every registered component has all required states and supported platform variants
All theme/token pairs pass contrast and no raw value or detached critical instance remains
Duplicate semantic components and stale major versions fail
Every D6 screen uses mapped published components or an approved expiring exception
Deliberate missing-state, duplicate and hardcoded-token fixtures fail
contracts_schema: Consumes design library/component/token and handoff manifests
security_privacy: Component examples use synthetic data
Redaction/privacy variants cannot be omitted
observability: Token gap, duplicate, detached instance, deprecated use and mapping coverage
rollout_rollback: Warn during initial import, required before D6
Rollback pins prior library and blocks new publication
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Design QA owns lint and fixtures; Design Systems owns corrections and cannot waive gate results.
definition_of_done: Required design-system gate operational
All negative fixtures pass

items.title: Implement design-to-code visual, interaction and semantic regression
items.outcome: Built Android, web and admin screens are compared with approved D6 artifacts for visual structure, interaction, semantics, content and states, with intentional deviations recorded.
items.context: A screenshot-only diff misses focus, labels, responsive behavior and state semantics. Build conformance begins with the first frontend pull request and gates release.
scope: Deterministic synthetic fixtures and presentation state
Deviation request, approval, expiry and baseline update
acceptance_criteria: Every implemented registered screen has screenshot and semantic baselines for required variants
Unexpected layout, token, component, copy, focus, state or interaction drift fails
Baseline updates require linked D6 artifact or approved deviation and cannot be accepted blindly
Sensitive values are synthetic and deterministic
T-QA-06, T-QA-08 and T-QA-13 consume the conformance result
contracts_schema: Conformance manifest links build, artifact, screen/state, fixture, baseline, result and deviation
security_privacy: No production screenshots or customer data
Artifacts and CI outputs follow retention/access policy
observability: Coverage, drift, flaky baseline, deviation age and platform failure
rollout_rollback: Enable per screen as implementation lands, required before D7/D8
Rollback pins previous approved baseline and blocks unreviewed change
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs for manifests and QA repositories for runners. Platform QA owns baselines; artifact authors approve only documented design changes.
definition_of_done: Conformance framework and platform pilots operational
Planted defects fail
QA, UX Engineering and CDO approvals recorded

items.title: Run cross-platform parity, UAT and release design QA
items.outcome: Release candidates pass persona-based UAT, approved parity/divergence, accessibility, localization, privacy and rollback design checks before private beta or public launch.
items.context: Per-platform QA can miss a cross-channel handoff or contradictory term. D8 verifies the assembled release and exact feature set.
scope: Android device, web browser/zoom and admin role matrices
Release evidence, defect threshold, waiver expiry and rollback comparison
acceptance_criteria: Every included critical journey passes on its supported platforms and cross-channel handoffs
Parity gaps are fixed or have CDO-approved user/job rationale
No open critical/high design, accessibility or abuse finding remains
Rollback preserves safe, understandable states and does not restore retired design
T-REL-02 and T-REL-03 consume unexpired D8 evidence
contracts_schema: UAT/release record links build, artifact versions, journeys, platforms, evidence, findings, decision and expiry
security_privacy: Synthetic release fixtures and least-privilege roles
No waiver for raw-content, money arithmetic, authorization or safe-exit invariants
observability: Journey pass rate, parity gap, defect age, waiver expiry and rollback result
rollout_rollback: Runs on each release candidate
Failed/expired D8 evidence prevents promotion
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs for UAT evidence; independent platform QA executes matrices and Release/Design leadership makes the final decision.
definition_of_done: Release UAT and parity pack complete
All blocking findings closed/retested

items.title: Run the cross-platform upfront design readiness gate
items.outcome: A single executable D6 gate proves every planned Android, customer-web and admin surface is researched, designed, validated, registered and handed off before frontend implementation becomes Ready.
items.context: The user requires the complete product experience up front. Individual platform approvals are necessary but do not prove cross-platform allocation, shared-system or traceability completeness.
scope: Heuristic, accessibility, usability, comprehension, privacy/abuse and system-lint evidence
acceptance_criteria: T-DQA-01 coverage check reports every frontend ticket mapped with zero dangling or missing owners
T-UXA-16, T-UXW-12 and T-UXM-11 are approved and reference one compatible design-system version
T-DQA-02 through T-DQA-09 have no open critical/high finding and evidence is unexpired
All required diagrams and D6 manifests are immutable and reviewer-accessible
CDO approval is recorded and every mapped frontend ticket depends on this gate plus its exact flow design
contracts_schema: schema/design-readiness.schema.json fixes artifact versions, platform approvals, check evidence, findings, exceptions, reviewer identities, expiry, decision and checksum
security_privacy: Evidence contains no real participant/financial data
No waiver can bypass core privacy, authorization, raw-content or money invariants
observability: Missing/stale evidence, open finding, approval age and frontend dependency coverage
tests: Expired approval and prohibited waiver failures
rollout_rollback: Required before any mapped frontend Ready; repository scaffolds and backend work remain independent
Material design change reopens only affected evidence and frontend dependencies
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Design QA assembles immutable evidence; platform leads own their packs and the CDO alone records the cross-platform readiness decision.
